title: How few crew seasons?

blocks.text: A pipeline firm hires inspection crews by the season. Each job is a whole number of crew-months that one crew must do whole, and a season holds `season` crew-months. How few seasons (crews) cover every job?

Write `fewest_crews(sizes, season)` in `packing.py`, as a MathOpt model. Return the number of seasons used and the jobs in each used season, as `(count, [[job indices], ...])`, or `None` when no packing exists.
The model, with $`B`$ the seasons offered, $`x_{i,b} = 1`$ when job $`i`$ goes in season $`b`$ and $`y_b = 1`$ when season $`b`$ is used:

Offer enough seasons that a packing always exists when every job fits in one season: one season per job, `len(sizes)` seasons in all, as the reference offers, is always enough (each job alone in its own season). Read the answer only when the solve is optimal, and return `None` otherwise (a job longer than the season makes the model infeasible). Return the count as an `int`, with `round(result.objective_value())`, and leave out the empty seasons from the list. Solve with `mathopt.SolverType.CP_SAT`. About fifteen lines.
